author: codex-root

patch.value: Roadmap horizon and promotion policy: outcome-based portfolio horizons with evidence-gated movement

Define one durable portfolio policy for organizing immediate foundations, scale expansion, universal-platform capabilities, and exploratory research without speculative calendar promises or duplicate initiative trees.

The policy defines Current, Emerging, Expansion, and Exploratory horizons by evidence and dependency readiness rather than dates; Every horizon entry references an existing canonical item or passes an all-status duplicate check before creation; Promotion requires explicit acceptance evidence, predecessor state, scale or quality proof where applicable, and an append-only decision comment; Demotion, splitting, merging, rejection, and supersedence preserve prior rationale in immutable history; Cross-cutting quality, security, documentation, SDK parity, graph completeness, and token-efficiency gates apply to every horizon; The living milestone can render a bounded horizon summary without replacing detailed item metadata or creating parallel backlogs
Keep the multi-decade roadmap understandable, adaptable, and traceable while every independently deliverable capability remains a canonical item
Agents and maintainers can see what matures next, why it is sequenced there, and what evidence promotes it without reading the full historical corpus
Reduces duplicate roadmap items, premature implementation, hidden prerequisites, and calendar-driven commitments while preserving ambitious future planning
A living outcome-based horizon map links canonical initiatives, promotion evidence, dependencies, risks, and review triggers from current foundations through long-term universal-platform research

The ecosystem now spans command simplification, SDK-first architecture, million-item context, graph analytics, immutable history, multi-agent safety, CI, VCS, digital twins, federation, signatures, and policy; the existing initiatives need one explicit promotion model.

Quality, security, documentation, immutable proof, and token budgets are continuous constraints rather than a separate terminal phase.

author: harness:claude-code
message: Typed strategic edge: connect the outcome ladder so milestone reachability is computable by graph traversal instead of inferred from untyped related edges

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Long-horizon planning pass 2026-07-26. This note argues for one addition to the horizon policy: the six outcome milestones under pm-doxj are a complete ladder for reaching v1.0 and the universal-platform claim, and they are all bounded by things this project controls. Nothing in the portfolio is horizoned against things it does not control, and for a tool whose stated target is workspaces spanning several decades, that is the gap worth naming before another milestone is ever considered.

Where the ladder currently ends. j82fd3 (grammar), 9rgaal (SDK-complete), w7ccmv (provable history), o87av6 (proven scale), xp1xsw (v1.0 GA), t4d7nz (universal domain platform). Each is falsifiable, each has an owner, and after the 2026-07-26 edge pass each is reachable from 268 of 271 active items through typed implements and verifies paths. The ladder is not missing a rung. What it is missing is a statement of what happens after the last rung, on a timescale where the assumptions underneath every rung stop holding.

Three decade-scale forces, each with a concrete near-term consequence that can be acted on now rather than planned for later.

1. The reader outlives the writer. pm-e5yupa already requires a declared support window per format version and a CI-proven reader for the oldest supported version. The decade-scale version of that requirement is stronger and cheaper to adopt now than later: the on-disk format should be readable by a program that has never seen this codebase. pm-4jk8kx (open workspace format specification with a conformance suite) is the item that makes that true, and its real justification is not interoperability with other tools today but readability by tools that do not exist yet. A workspace whose only reader is this binary is a workspace with a 5-to-10 year life, whatever the support policy says. Recommend promoting pm-4jk8kx's horizon on the strength of that argument rather than on the interoperability argument currently recorded.

2. The consumer changes shape faster than the storage. Every token-efficiency decision in this portfolio - budgets (pm-5t33or), encodings (pm-kvxqp1), projections (pm-cxr0jb), packing (pm-4k6b) - is calibrated against the context windows and tokenizers of current coding agents. Those will change by orders of magnitude, in both directions, over the life of a decade-scale workspace: windows grow, but so does the number of agents sharing one budget. The durable form of this work is therefore not any particular budget number but the mechanism that lets budgets be re-derived: pm-t5dt4z (self-reported token accounting) and pm-8pnj (tokens per completed task as a CI-visible metric) are the two items that survive a tenfold change in consumer shape. Every hardcoded ceiling is a dated artifact. Recommend that the horizon policy classify budget numbers as explicitly dated and re-derivable, and classify the instruments that produce them as long-horizon.

3. Immutability is a claim about the future, so it must be verifiable without us. w7ccmv makes history immutably recorded and independently verifiable. pm-3z0k (portable integrity attestation - export a detached proof bundle, verify it standalone) is what makes "independently" literally true: a third party with the bundle and no pm installation can confirm the record was not altered. On a decade scale that is the difference between a tamper-evidence claim and a tamper-evidence fact, because the party who needs to check will not be running this version of this tool. pm-3z0k currently sits at priority 3. Its priority is defensible on near-term value and understates its horizon value; recommend the horizon policy record that distinction rather than resolving it by re-prioritizing, since near-term sequencing should stay driven by near-term value.

The policy addition this note proposes, in one sentence: every portfolio item carries a horizon classification that is independent of its priority, where priority answers "when should this be worked on" and horizon answers "how long will this decision bind", and items whose horizon exceeds their priority - pm-4jk8kx, pm-3z0k, pm-e5yupa, pm-4020c5, and the format and vocabulary decisions generally - are flagged so that a cheap decision made today is not allowed to bind a workspace for twenty years without anyone noticing it was a twenty-year decision.

Why no seventh outcome milestone. The three forces above do not describe a new outcome; they describe durability constraints on outcomes that already exist. A "decade-scale durability" milestone would overlap w7ccmv and t4d7nz and would dilute a ladder whose current strength is that every rung is falsifiable. The correct home is this policy item and the horizon field it governs.
